title: Two birch ply wardrobes either side of a passage
summary: A two-door and a three-door wardrobe facing each other across a passage, with birch ply sides and doors and Sandy Birch boxes inside.
intro: Two wardrobes either side of the short passage to a door: one with three doors, one with two. The side panels and doors are 18 mm birch ply finished with Osmo oil, and the boxes inside are Sandy Birch melamine, close enough in colour that the whole thing reads as one wood. Each stands on its own timber base, and the wall side was fitted tight by cutting back the skirting.

steps.title: Two empty corners
steps.text: A wide landing in Stoke Newington, with a corner each side of the short passage to a door. The plan was a wardrobe in each, facing each other across the passage.

image.alt: The empty room before the work, a bare corner beside the doorway

steps.title: Bases first
steps.text: Each wardrobe stands on its own timber base, set out on the floor and levelled first, so the boxes go on something flat and true whatever the floor is doing.

image.alt: Two timber base frames laid out on the floor either side of the doorway

steps.title: Boxes in Sandy Birch
steps.text: The boxes are made from Sandy Birch melamine board, which is very close in colour to birch ply, so the inside matches the outside. They were built on the floor, then stood up.

image.alt: A wardrobe box being put together on the floor, with tools beside it

steps.title: Stood up on the bases
steps.text: Each box is stood up and slid back onto its base, against the wall.

image.alt: An empty wardrobe box standing on its base in the corner

steps.title: Birch ply outside
steps.text: The outer shell is 18 mm birch ply: the side panels and the doors. The birch ply is finished with Osmo oil, which keeps it looking like raw wood.

image.alt: Both wardrobes with their birch ply sides, either side of the passage

steps.title: Tight against the wall
steps.text: The tricky part was the side panel on the wall side. It was very tight, so the skirting came off along that wall, was cut back, and went back on so the panel fits neatly.

image.alt: The two-door wardrobe tight against the wall, with the skirting cut round it

steps.title: Inside
steps.text: The three-door wardrobe has a tall run of shelves behind one door and hanging with shelves under it behind the other two. The two-door wardrobe has a top shelf, a hanging rail and low shelves.

image.alt: The three-door wardrobe open: shelves on the left, hanging rail and low shelves on the right

steps.title: Handles on
steps.text: Soft close hinges on every door, and long dark bar handles to finish.

image.alt: The three-door wardrobe finished with its bar handles, next to the door

model3d.title: The wardrobes in 3D
model3d.text: Both wardrobes drawn in 3D facing each other across the passage, with the same insides as the real ones. Nothing was measured for the page, so the sizes are standard: 1500 and 1200 mm wide, 2400 mm high and 600 mm deep. Open the doors, or take them apart.
